assessment_summary: I validated the URBO 'workspace' instance against the guide's expectations by inspecting state and exercising live behavior. (1) Prerequisites: node/pnpm/just/JDK/Docker all installed at the versions claimed. (2) Instance state: .urbo-instance='workspace', .urbo/workspace/ holds env, generated nginx.conf, ports.json, realm-hash and a seeded marker (2026-10-18T19:31Z). (3) Containers: all 9 compose services + shared proxy up; health checks pass; the seeder (sample-data-loader) exited 0 with 'Sample data import completed successfully'. (4) End-to-end HTTP: the sandbox resolver does not special-case .localhost (as the installer noted), so I hit the proxy at 127.0.0.1:80 with matching Host headers for each hostname. All three dev-server frontends returned their real app HTML (UrboApp, Urbo-CMS, SteleBoards) with Vite serving modules; the API hostname reaches the Spring Boot backend which returned seeded JSON for /v1/events and /v1/feed-configuration; Keycloak served the swcode realm's OIDC metadata, JWK certs and login page, with issuer exactly matching the backend's resource-server config in the instance env (the guide's key invariant: identical issuer between browser and backend); Meilisearch, imgproxy, Mailpit, LocalStack and sample-images all answered correctly through the proxy. (5) Data: Postgres urbo DB has 171 tables with seeded rows (11 events, 20 categories, 10 citizen services). (6) Orchestration: just status and just urls work and agree with the guide. Two limitations were noted: (a) 'just doctor' fails the GITHUB_TOKEN preflight in a fresh shell because the token was only exported during the install session, not persisted to a shell profile — this gates only a future backend image rebuild (the built image already exists and is serving), and the installer had empirically verified a dummy token suffices since all build dependencies resolve from public repos; (b) host memory is tight (7.6 GiB, ~256 MiB available, historical OOM kills in dmesg), which matches the installer's own caveat that dev servers can die under pressure — at validation time all three dev servers were running and responding. Neither limitation reflects an incomplete installation; every component the guide describes (proxy, infra, backend, seeded data, three dev apps, Keycloak auth) is present and demonstrably operational.
